rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials ended off track (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.11 to 0.16, and max_error (0.061 to 0.067) reached the 0.06 m off-track limit in every case. RMS error was small (about 0.03), so the robot tracked the line closely until a sudden excursion. Each run lost the line once, and steering oscillation was 0.07 to 0.16. The failure pattern points to an aggressive steering loop: kp = 4 gives a full-scale differential of about 1400 PWM at signal 1, and kd = 0.3 is too weak to damp the swing, so the robot overshoots at bends, loses the tape, and leaves the track. The sensors are also tight (x of +/-0.04 m, 12 mm footprints), so the outer sensors drop off the tape early on sharper bends. Changes: (1) kp 4.0 -> 3.0 to soften the steering response and reduce overshoot; (2) kd 0.3 -> 0.9 to damp the change in signal; (3) ki 0.05 -> 0.02 to limit integral windup on bends; (4) base_speed 1.6 -> 1.4 so the robot can make the bends at speed, accepting some risk on the 3 s finish time; (5) sensor x spread widened to +/-0.03 m with a 5-sensor layout (x = 0.03, 0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03) for earlier warning of drift, and kept at y = 0.05 m; (6) body mass 0.8 -> 0.6 kg to reduce yaw inertia so the robot responds faster to the steering. Expected result: fewer off-track exits, with progress rising above 0.5 on at least the oval and s-bend. The finish time may still be marginal. Hypotheses: (a) the off-track exits come from overshoot at bends caused by kp and kd, not from sensor coverage; (b) base_speed of 1.4 may be too slow to finish in 3 s; (c) line loss occurs at the sharpest bend when the outer sensors go blank. Next measurements I want: progress and completion per track, max_error and where it occurs, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation, so I can tell whether the damping change worked and whether speed or tracking limits the finish.
